scope: CPU availability and API latency assessment; actual deployed staging, read-only production context

method.clientLocation: local workstation outside VPS, public staging HTTPS
method.protocol: HTTP/1.1, a new connection per request, gzip requested
method.warmup: one excluded initial request per case; no cache flush or database-page purge
method.percentiles: nearest rank, ceil(0.95*n)-1; all 100 success observations retained
method.cases: same group/project pinned for first four routes; separate code 5719 reference project
method.cpuGuard: pause dispatch after five sampled steal values >=50%, resume after five <35%; no pause actually triggered
method.dataSafety: normal GETs and normal login/logout/session/access bookkeeping; response bodies hashed and discarded, no business edit

findings.finding: 100 successful responses per case completed for five cases. Cards p95 2225.98ms misses the 2000ms target; reference project5719 p95 1556.20ms is slightly above1500ms. Point summary p953532.74ms is the slowest measured surface; the plan has no separate point p95 threshold.

CPU steal remains above the below5% target both without synthetic load and during the gentle API cohort. After the observed archive container was no longer running, steal median was still17.90%, with host idle median59.61%.

The archive container used its existing0.5CPU quota and other services were active. Local competition contributes context; the persistent steal after the archive container disappeared does not support attributing all unavailability to that job. No backup was altered.

Staging API has no Docker CPU/memory cap and its jobs-in-API variable is absent (application defaulttrue). Production API is limited to1.5CPU/2GiB and runs with jobs disabled in API. Staging cgroup memory peaked2359222272B (~2.20GiB) during the four-route cohort, above the production cgroup limit; the later snapshot fell to~0.99GiB. The observation measures cgroup totals, and Node heap budgeting depends on the configured limit; equivalent budgets still need validation.
No filtroAPP OOM increments were observed. Initial host MemAvailable was9298060KiB and I/O wait median1.09%. Short windows do not exclude every database/I/O bottleneck.

Production source is the prior calendar implementation and its cache master flag is false. Its natural route statistics are separate from current staging. Cumulative SQL leaders include COPY backups; top-query counters recorded no new calls in the compared later interval. Historical COPY times are not attributed to current page queries.

nextActions.action: Ask hosting provider to check vCPU scheduling/availability and any host-level limit using both idle-context and measured-cohort UTC series. Guest data does not identify the specific physical-host cause.
nextActions.status: evidence and ticket text prepared; no message sent

nextActions.action: Align staging HTTP/worker topology, pool and resource limits with production; make sync-staging stop/start the worker safely without changing backup generation, backup retention or historical data. Recheck memory and latency with equivalent budgets.

Compare response-only cache with the same four-route workload and a browser-like persistent connection protocol, then profile the cold point/cards calculation with stable CPU before choosing another code optimization. Preserve all financial/history fields.
nextActions.status: next staging comparison; flags not changed

nextActions.action: Complete viewer/division/after-write/concurrent coverage and production24h/seven-day monitoring after manual rollout; this single-administrator low-rate measurement does not close those gates.

limitations: Measured API p95 is available; it is an observation at0.5requests/s and concurrency1, not a stress test or production acceptance.
A new HTTPS connection is opened per request. Browser HTTP/2/keepalive reuse is not reproduced, and this overhead can matter for the small56ms miss on the reference-project target.
Sequential cohorts have different host load and different route mixes. Their medians/p95 are not an isolated before/after effect of code or cache.
Staging resource limits/background-job topology differ from production; no claim that these results predict production within its1.5CPU/2GiB limits.
Current published staging uses monthly cache only; response/reference/progress flags are disabled. No flag, service, quota or schedule was modified for this assessment.
Only one administrator and one group/project plus the5719 reference project. Financial payload hashes were stable per case; no viewer/business-write invalidation test performed.
CPU snapshots are sixty samples each; API-window infrastructure series are longer but still not24-hour/seven-day observation.
pg_stat_statements aggregates are cumulative, and staging extension is not preloaded. No extension install, stats reset, database configuration or SQL tuning was performed.

HostStealAtStartPercent in raw client rows is the most recent sample checked before the dispatch delay and can be up to roughly two seconds older than actual start. Summary CPU metrics use measured-window timestamps.
